items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: Buddy and I had made so many records together. You know, Buck and Buddy, Buck and Buddy Blues.

ctx.x: Yes, we had Lester and Buddy Tate was no Herschel was gone because Buddy was out in California. And then we'd shoot down to Los Angeles and make a picture. We made a couple of pictures and we were making these little, little movies that you put a quarter in. But we did quite a few movies, you know. Hit Parade of 1942 or something like that. Reveille at Beverley. Those, that we made.
And records were going pretty well?

items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: There’s Sweets and Buck. Vic Dickenson, Dan Minor.

ctx.x: There’s a story I remember traveling with Basie and at that time they traveled on the trains and this is when they had the berth that you could sleep in. And then you’d have, every morning the wives with the kids of all the musicians would come and we’d come to breakfast. And there was Snooky, played the trumpet with Basie at the time, and then Earle Warren, and I’d have names for all of them. Well musicians have names for each other, Smiley, and Sweets —
